PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Indication for Testing: Prenatal amniocentesis sample testing
Gestational Age at Sampling: [redacted] weeks
Reason for Referral: Common chromosomal trisomy screening

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniocytes to detect common aneuploidies. DNA was extracted from amniotic fluid cells and amplified using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y. A minimum of four informative markers were analyzed per chromosome. PCR products were separated by capillary electrophoresis and analyzed using GeneMapper software. Peak area ratios between 0.8-1.4 were considered normal (disomic), while ratios <0.65 or >1.8 indicated aneuploidy.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13:
Markers tested: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
Result: Normal disomic pattern observed
Peak ratios: All within normal range (0.95-1.12)

Chromosome 18:
Markers tested: D18S391, D18S390, D18S535, D18S386
Result: Normal disomic pattern observed
Peak ratios: All within normal range (0.89-1.08)

Chromosome 21:
Markers tested: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1446
Result: Normal disomic pattern observed
Peak ratios: All within normal range (0.91-1.15)

Sex Chromosomes:
AMELOGENIN: XY pattern detected
Result: Male fetus

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates a normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormalities detected. The results are consistent with a chromosomally normal male fetus for the tested chromosomes.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y only. This test cannot detect:
- Chromosomal mosaicism below 20%
- Segmental imbalances or structural rearrangements
- Aneuploidies of other chromosomes
- Single gene disorders
- Maternal cell contamination below detectable levels

RECOMMENDATIONS
Proceed with full chromosome analysis by conventional karyotyping or chromosomal microarray to exclude other chromosomal abnormalities not detectable by QF-PCR. Results should be interpreted in conjunction with ultrasound findings and other clinical information.
